preserve_assertions.crates_is_product_code: crates/** is ADOPTER-OWNED product Rust (e.g. rev_scraping, contact_dev). It MUST be preserved and never overwritten by a harness sync. For the harness-OWNED harness-rust/crates/** runtime, see the harness_rust_distribution assertion — under the current Option X it is governed by neither this preserve entry nor any managed glob.
preserve_assertions.harness_rust_distribution: harness-rust/crates/** is the harness-OWNED semantic runtime, distinct from adopter product crates/**. Under the current and recommended Option X, adopters reference rev_harness's launcher (scripts/launch-semantic-mcp.sh) and build/run rev_harness's own harness-rust crate on the fly, so harness-rust/** is intentionally absent from BOTH managed_candidate_globs (never blind-copied) AND preserve_globs (not adopter-owned). Per-adopter crate-sync distribution (Option Y, fully self-contained, for client distribution) is a future track that, when adopted, adds harness-rust/** to managed_candidate_globs; tracked in task #25.
preserve_assertions.dual_lgtm_state_never_excluded: .agent/state/dual_lgtm_state.json is I-3 dual-LGTM evidence. It is PRESERVE/evidence and MUST NEVER appear in any exclude_globs or blind-overwrite/managed set. Only runtime lock residue under .agent/state/ may be excluded.

client_distribution.exclude_assertion_dual_lgtm_never_exclud: .agent/state/dual_lgtm_state.json is I-3 evidence and is intentionally ABSENT from exclude_globs. Only .agent/state/*.lock, *.lock.d/**, and locks/** runtime residue are excluded; the blanket .agent/state/** is never excluded so dual_lgtm_state.json always ships/preserves.
client_distribution.semantic_db_regeneration: Regenerate only after explicit semantic addon enablement from .shared/project_id through scripts/launch-semantic-mcp.sh, scripts/semantic-bootstrap.sh, or an explicit reindex workflow. Core-only setup and doctor do not create semantic DB state.

managed_candidate_globs_semantics: TIER-1 HARNESS-OWNED: blind-overwrite/replace on sync. These are harness-authored and carry no per-adopter state. NOTE: .codex/config.toml is deliberately EXCLUDED from this set (see managed_candidate_exclude_globs + merge_globs); a blind copy would destroy the per-adopter absolute `command =` launcher path, the §9 6-tool approval allowlist, and the I-13 canonical key.
merge_globs_semantics: TIER-2 TEMPLATED/MERGE — never blind-overwrite. These files carry per-adopter state that a copy would clobber; the sync executor must structurally merge (e.g. TOML-structural merge for .codex/config.toml), never `cp`. .codex/config.toml specifically must preserve: (1) the per-adopter absolute `command =` launcher path, (2) the §9 6-tool approval allowlist, (3) the I-13 canonical key. .codex/config.toml is narrowed OUT of managed_candidate_globs via managed_candidate_exclude_globs and listed here instead.
